Because it was the largest vessel floating at the time, and because it was one of only three Olympic class vessels. These vessels used a system of isolated compartments (16 total) that extended well above the waterline. The lower portions would be sealed off automatically in the event of an emergency, so the hull would still be displacing more than its mass, keeping the main deck about the waves.

When this system was designed, the expected hull rupture would have been a relatively small hole. But the iceberg dragged along the hull, tearing open more of the water-tight compartments than would be able to keep the ship afloat. The reason the Titanic gets so much press is because Its sister ship. the RMS Olympic, did not sink. The third and last-built Olympic class vessel, the RMS Brittanic, sank due to an external explosion, either a depth charge or torpedo.
